title: Fourier Entropy–Influence conjecture
area: Communication complexity and Boolean function analysis
formal: Does there exist one finite real constant \(C>0\) such that, for every positive integer \(n\) and every function \(f:\{-1,1\}^{n}\to\{-1,1\}\), \[H(f)\le C I(f),\] where \(H(f)\) is the Shannon entropy in bits of the squared Fourier spectrum and \(I(f)\) is total influence for uniformly distributed inputs? The same \(C\) must work for all dimensions and all Boolean functions.
definitions: Let \([n]=\{1,\ldots,n\}\) and give each \(x\in\{-1,1\}^n\) probability \(2^{-n}\). For \(S\subseteq[n]\), define \(\chi_S(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i\), with empty product one, and \[\widehat f(S)=2^{-n}\sum_{x\in\{-1,1\}^n}f(x)\chi_S(x),\qquad q_S=\widehat f(S)^2.\] These are real coefficients and \(\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}q_S=1\). Define \(\eta(0)=0\) and \(\eta(t)=t\log_2(1/t)\) for \(0<t\le1\), where \(\log_2 t=\ln t/\ln2\). Then \[H(f)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}\eta(q_S).\] The sum includes the empty set and is not conditioned on nonempty spectral subsets or divided by the variance. For each \(i\in[n]\), let \(x^{\oplus i}\) negate coordinate \(i\) and retain all other coordinates. Set \[I_i(f)=2^{-n}\bigl|\{x\in\{-1,1\}^n:f(x)\ne f(x^{\oplus i})\}\bigr|,\qquad I(f)=\sum_{i=1}^n I_i(f)=\sum_{S\subseteq[n]}|S|q_S.\] Influence uses an actual bit flip, with no additional probability of leaving that coordinate unchanged. All scalar Boolean functions are allowed; no balance, monotonicity, circuit-size, degree or efficient-computability promise is imposed. Constant functions satisfy \(H(f)=I(f)=0\). The inequality is non-strict, so it includes them.
answer_criterion: Provide a complete mathematically correct proof checked in Lean of the universal inequality for some positive finite constant, or of its logical negation. A positive proof must use the specified uniform measure, full squared spectrum, base-two Shannon entropy and total bit-flip influence for every \(n\) and every scalar Boolean function. A negative proof must establish \[\forall C>0\ \exists n\ge1\ \exists f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\},\quad H(f)>C I(f).\] The dimension and function may depend on \(C\); equivalently, the entropy-to-influence ratios of nonconstant Boolean functions must be unbounded. Defeating one numerical constant or checking finitely many truth tables is insufficient. No optimal value of \(C\), algorithm for finding counterexamples or numerical approximation is required.
why: A central structural conjecture connecting sensitivity to spectral information. Its resolution would sharpen our understanding of Boolean functions and spectral learning, while testing a relation that fails without the Boolean constraint.

importance.reason: A longstanding, broadly consequential conjecture in Boolean function analysis, with direct learning-theory implications and active 2026 progress that still leaves the universal classical inequality open.

progress.text: Friedgut and Kalai propose FEI; the historical attribution is recorded in the checked O’Donnell–Wright–Zhou primary paper.
O’Donnell, Wright and Zhou establish the symmetric and read-once decision-tree cases and detail the consequence for fixed-accuracy DNF Fourier concentration.
Keller, Mossel and Schlank post the coordinate binary-entropy upper bound in Claim 4.1.
Han’s bound with an additional coordinate-entropy term appears online in Combinatorica; the journal volume is dated 2025.
Li and Han withdraw their weaker-bound refinement, citing the result already present in Keller–Mossel–Schlank Claim 4.1.
Xiao Han’s v2 adds a note acknowledging related earlier work.
González, MacManus and Pereyra revise results for \(\delta\)-tribes and separated classes while retaining the unrestricted conjecture.
Slote reports a quantum counterexample with quadratic entropy and linear influence in its degree parameter; it does not settle scalar Boolean FEI.
Slote, Volberg and Zhang revise further quantum examples, including bounded influence with growing Pauli entropy, and explicitly retain the classical question.

status_note: Open in the checked classical primary literature, explicitly reiterated in both August 2026 quantum papers. Bounded searches and version checks through 15 September 2026 found no proof or refutation of the universal scalar Boolean Shannon-entropy inequality. The June separated classes impose extra hypotheses, the coordinate-entropy estimates retain an extra term, and the August counterexamples are operator-valued or use non-Boolean complex phases. Li–Han’s December 2025 weaker-bound preprint was withdrawn for prior appearance of its result. Complete new preprint proofs were not independently verified.

context_blocks.text: A Fourier coefficient records correlation with a parity of selected input bits. Squaring these correlations gives a probability distribution on subsets of the coordinates. Its Shannon entropy measures dispersion among subsets; total influence is the expected cardinality of a subset from that distribution. The conjecture asks whether being the spectrum of a Boolean-valued function forces a universal linear relation between these two quantities.

This is not a generic fact about probability distributions on subsets. A distribution uniform on the n singleton sets has entropy \(\log _{2} n\) but expected set size one. It is the squared Fourier spectrum of the normalized real function \(g(x)=(x_{1}+\cdots +x_{n})/\sqrt{n}\), which is generally not Boolean. Conversely, a parity of all n inputs has entropy zero and total influence n. These examples explain both why Boolean-valuedness matters and why the proposed inequality has only one direction.

If FEI holds with constant \(C\), then for every \(0<\delta<1\), some family \(\mathcal T\) of at most \(2^{CI(f)/\delta}\) subsets satisfies \(\sum_{S\notin\mathcal T}q_S\le\delta\). Equivalently, retaining those Fourier coefficients approximates \(f\) with mean squared error at most \(\delta\) under the uniform measure. The support bound depends on the accuracy parameter; a guarantee independent of accuracy is not being asserted.

O’Donnell, Wright and Zhou prove FEI for symmetric Boolean functions, which are invariant under every permutation of coordinates, and for read-once decision trees, where the variables used in the two branches at each query are disjoint. The read-once condition is stronger than merely avoiding a repeated query along each path. Their application to a disjunction of \(m\ge2\) conjunctions of literals uses \(I(f)=O(\log m)\): FEI would give concentration on \(m^{O(1/\delta)}\) Fourier coefficients for each fixed error \(\delta\). This is a version of Mansour’s conjecture, not its stronger proposed logarithmic dependence on inverse error. It concerns uniform-measure spectral concentration and the associated query-learning setting.

Han’s Theorem 1 bounds \(H(f)\) by an absolute constant times \(I(f)+\sum_i I_i(f)\log_2(1/I_i(f))\), with zero terms when \(I_i(f)=0\). The journal version appeared online on 20 December 2024 in Combinatorica volume 45 (2025). The 10 December 2025 arXiv revision adds an acknowledgement of related prior work by Keller, Mossel and Schlank. The extra coordinate-entropy term can exceed a constant times total influence, so this bound leaves FEI open.

The earlier Keller–Mossel–Schlank paper already gives \(H(f)\le\sum_i h_2(I_i(f))\) in Claim 4.1, where \(h_2(t)=-t\log_2 t-(1-t)\log_2(1-t)\) with zero endpoint terms. The claim supplies the same general kind of coordinate-entropy control and applies beyond Boolean-valued spectra after normalization. This is why a later proof or refinement of that weaker bound must be distinguished from resolving FEI. Min-entropy, \(-\log_2\max_S q_S\), concerns just the largest coefficient and is a different, weaker target than Shannon entropy.

González, MacManus and Pereyra’s revision of 9 June 2026 reports FEI for the defined \(\delta\)-tribes class and for classes with recursive separation properties. The separation theorems retain hypotheses on their terminal functions and constants; they are not assertions for all monotone functions or unrestricted decision trees. The paper also exhibits failure of a stronger inequality involving a prescribed splitting coordinate. Those examples satisfy FEI, so that failure is not a counterexample to this card’s target.

Slote’s 2 August 2026 preprint reports a counterexample to the quantum extension, whose inputs are Hermitian unitary operators and whose coefficients come from tensor products of Pauli matrices. Theorems 1 and 5 give operators supported on degree-\(d\) Pauli terms with entropy \(\Theta(d^2)\) and influence \(d\). Classical Boolean functions form a restricted diagonal case of that operator setting. The operators constructed in the theorem therefore do not supply scalar Boolean counterexamples. The full new construction was not independently verified in this review.

A follow-up by Slote, Volberg and Zhang, revised 6 August 2026, also treats quantum counterexamples. Its §6.6 reports Hermitian involutions with total influence below two and spectral entropy \(\log_2 n+O(1)\) in its family parameter. The underlying auxiliary scalar functions take complex values of modulus one, rather than only the real values \(-1\) and \(1\). That domain change is essential, and §6 still describes classical FEI as open. These theorem scopes were checked without independently certifying the full proofs.

A positive solution would expose a strong restriction on the spectra of every Boolean computation, independently of how that computation is represented. A negative solution would identify Boolean functions whose spectral information greatly exceeds their sensitivity to input changes. Either outcome would clarify a basic link between combinatorial stability, harmonic analysis and the possibility of learning from sparse spectral descriptions.
